questions.q: Of what material did Bezalel make the box?
questions.a: Bezalel made the box of acacia wood.

questions.q: Why did Bezalel put the poles into the rings on the sides of the box?
questions.a: He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the box in order to carry the ark.

questions.q: Which direction did the cherubim face?
questions.a: The cherubim faced each another and looked toward the center of the atonement lid.

questions.q: What objects would be on the table?
questions.a: The dishes, spoons, the bowls, and pitchers to be used to pour out the offerings would be on the table.

questions.q: What was located on each branch extending out from the lampstand?
questions.a: Each branch had three cups made like almond blossoms, with a leafy base and a flower, and three cups made like almond blossoms in the other branch, with a leafy base and a flower.

questions.q: How much gold did Bezalel use to make the lampstand and its accessories?
questions.a: He made the lampstand and its accessories with one talent of pure gold.
A border of gold surrounded the incense altar.

questions.q: Who made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense?
questions.a: Bezalel made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense.

commentary.text: The making of the ark, and the furniture of the tabernacle.

—In the furniture of the tabernacle were emblems of a spiritual and acceptable service. The incense represented the prayers of the saints. The sacrifice of the alter represented the Lamb of God that taketh away the sins of the world. The golden pot with manna, or bread from heaven, the flesh of Jesus Christ, which he gave for the life of the world. The candlestick, with its lights, the teaching and enlightening of the Holy Spirit. The shew-bread represented that provision for those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, which the gospel, the ordinances and the sacraments of the house of prayer, abundantly bestow. The exactness of the workmen to their rule, should be followed by us; seeking for the influences of the Holy Spirit, that we may rejoice in and glorify God while in this world, and at length be with him for ever.
